name: Exactly-one-face ambient population order and Pythagorean scale mechanism
equation: For primitive canonical R<=B cuboids with exactly one integral face and no space condition, M1(B) asymp B^2 log B and M1(B)/U(B) asymp log(B)/B. The power drop comes from replacing one free edge-pair by scaled primitive Pythagorean faces; the logarithm comes from the harmonic face-scale sum.

name: Canonical exactly-one directional chamber asymptotic and non-2:1:1 limit law
equation: For primitive canonical integral-space cuboids 0<a<b<c with exactly one integral face and d<=B, N_q(B) ~ [kappa I_q/(3*pi^3)] B(log B)^3 for q in {ab,ac,bc}, where on R={0<x<y<z in S^2}, I_ab=int_R dω/sqrt(x^2+y^2), I_ac=int_R dω/sqrt(x^2+z^2), I_bc=int_R dω/sqrt(y^2+z^2), and I_ab+I_ac+I_bc=pi^2/8. Hence N1(B)~[kappa/(24*pi)]B(log B)^3 and N_vec/N1 -> (8/pi^2)(I_ab,I_ac,I_bc)=(0.5347369332...,0.2453591778...,0.2199038889...), so the finite near-2:1:1 pattern is not the limiting law.
